text:
Bobby McMann scored 29 goals last season, a year split between Toronto and Seattle. This season he has three in 21 games and none in his last 14, and it would be easy to read that as a 30-year-old who has lost his touch.

Our numbers don't see it that way. He's still getting to his chances: 2.7 expected goals on his own shots over his last ten, right on his usual rate, and 50 shots on the season. Three goals on 5.3 expected is a drought, not a decline, and droughts like that usually end. His point rate (1.17 per 60) is far below his talent range. The bigger worry is five on five, where Seattle takes 41% of the expected goals with him on, nearly seven points worse than without him. He still plays hard (45 hits), and All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) says his offense lives in transition, 53% of his shots off the rush. Undrafted and once in the ECHL, he's been here before. Our range projects 17 to 31 goals.
